transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Atlas Head of MLOps), Evan (Atlas CTO), Marta (Platform), Ben (SRE), Noah (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot economics, review of last week's token/sec-$ numbers, caching observed savings, and proposed batching tradeoffs to push down unit cost while meeting 95th percentile latency SLOs. Agreed to run longer steady-state tests and a tail-latency deep dive.

Topics:
- tokens/sec/$ baseline and recent changes
- prefix/KV caching impact measured last 48h
- batching modes: continuous vs fixed-window vs three-tier bucket
- model variant and quantization tradeoffs
- deployment mode considerations (dedicated vs hosted for production)

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Maya (Redwood AE): ok hey everyone thanks for joining. quick agenda, we'll go through econ numbers, caching experiment results, then batching tradeoffs and next steps. priya, you had some updates on traffic?
[00:00:18] Priya (Atlas): yeah thanks maya. basically we ran the traffic replay for 36 hours, it's a mix of short QA prompts and longer multi-turn sessions. p50 is pretty low but p95 spikes are concerning, we saw a few bursts around noon pacific.
[00:00:33] Carlos (Redwood SE): got it. before we jump in, quick note: the config we used for the last run was redwood-hosted gpt-like-xxl quantized on int8, continuous batching with max batch size 64 and idle timeout 20ms, prefix cache turned on for the top 10 intents.
[00:00:47] Evan (Atlas): sorry can you repeat that, the int8 variant was on hosted? we thought the dedicated pool used int4?
[00:00:54] Carlos (Redwood SE): yeah, the hosted pilot used int8. dedicated pool proposal on our side can include int4-but we recommended a validation pass since we saw some small regression on long-horizon completions with int4 in the last lab run.
[00:01:07] Priya (Atlas): that's the concern — quality regression. our success criteria includes <=1% hallucination increase and <=2% latency degradation.
[00:01:15] Maya (Redwood AE): noted. ok let's look at the numbers. I shared the cost model earlier — baseline tokens/sec per dollar for your traffic (no cache) was about 12.5k tokens per dollar for the unquantized variant, switching to int8 bumped that to ~23k tokens/$, and with prefix cache on the top intents we observed an effective 1.9x improvement to about 44k tokens/$.
[00:01:42] Noah (Atlas ML Eng): wait that 1.9x — that's averaged across sessions including long form? curious how much came from short intents vs prefix reuse.
[00:01:52] Carlos (Redwood SE): yes it's averaged. short intents (<=30 tokens) have almost 80% cache hit rate for the top 10 intents. the long multi-turns have lower hits but the KV cache still reduces KV-regen cost by ~20% on average.
[00:02:06] Ben (SRE): how are you measuring cost? is this tokens billed or tokens generated+input? we need to match our internal accounting.
[00:02:12] Maya (Redwood AE): good call ben — in our model we bill based on generated + input tokens depending on route config. I uploaded two tabs: Atlas_accounting_input_only.csv and Atlas_accounting_total.csv, see assumptions column. we'll align on the SSO-level billing mapping in the next doc.
[00:02:26] Priya (Atlas): ok makes sense. on the latency side, we saw p95 ~ 420ms for short flows when cache hits occur, but non-hit short flows were 780ms p95 which pushes us over our 700ms SLO.
[00:02:41] Carlos (Redwood SE): that's where batching tradeoffs come in. continuous batching reduces per-token cost but can increase tail latency for low-concurrency bursts because of batch-assembly delays. the three-tier bucket approach we prototyped puts small, medium, and large requests into separate lanes with different max batch sizes and timeouts. that lowered p95 for short non-hit flows to ~610ms in our test.
[00:03:01] Marta (Atlas Platform): three-tier sounds promising. what's the tokens/sec/$ impact vs continuous? we care about unit cost too.
[00:03:09] Carlos (Redwood SE): tradeoff: continuous gave 1.0x baseline cost (lets call that 23k tokens/$ with int8), three-tier was about 0.86x cost (so ~27k tokens/$) — meaning slightly higher cost but improved p95. fixed-window batching with small window (10ms) was 0.93x cost but didn't fix the p95 spike as reliably.
[00:03:29] Evan (Atlas CTO): is that 27k tokens/$ after caching? or before?
[00:03:33] Carlos (Redwood SE): that was before prefix caching. with prefix caching applied we saw three-tier move to ~52k tokens/$ (effective) for your workload. continuous with cache was nearer ~44k tokens/$. so cache amplifies batching improvements.
[00:03:48] Priya (Atlas): interesting. can you break the numbers by workload segment? we need to justify cost to finance.
[00:03:54] Maya (Redwood AE): yes, in the spreadsheet we added three segments: short intents (40% of calls), medium (35%), long (25%). short intents drive most cache wins: with cache + three-tier short intents reach ~120k tokens/$ while long sessions are nearer 14k tokens/$. blended is that ~52k number.
[00:04:10] Noah (Atlas ML Eng): on the cache side, what's the eviction policy? we saw cold-starts after redeploys.
[00:04:16] Carlos (Redwood SE): TTL-based with LRU for per-model prefix store. for the pilot we used a 12-hour TTL and increase of hits plateaued after ~8 hours. redeploys clear the in-memory cache; persistent KV cache is an option if you need cross-instance reuse — adds small storage cost but big hit on cold-starts.
[00:04:33] Ben (SRE): how much storage and cost for persistent KV? ballpark?
[00:04:37] Carlos (Redwood SE): for your top 10 intents it's negligible, like a few hundred MB and a few dollars a month; for a larger prefix set (top 1k) you can be in low hundreds of dollars depending on your replication policy.
[00:04:50] Priya (Atlas): ok good. the other item — tail latency deep dive we asked for. what data do you need from us to reproduce the spikes?
[00:04:58] Maya (Redwood AE): sample traffic trace (we asked for 4 weeks), plus p99 traces correlated with infra metrics (GPU utilization, queue length). if you can share a 1-hour window where you observed spikes, we can run a deterministic replay and reproduce.
[00:05:14] Marta (Atlas): I'll extract a few 1-hour windows and upload them to the shared folder.
[00:05:18] Priya (Atlas): also curious about model variant fallback — if we push for int4 on dedicated do we have automatic fallback to int8 on quality regression?
[00:05:27] Carlos (Redwood SE): yes our rollout rules support model variant fallback on metric regression. you can pin canary traffic to int4 and ramp based on quality evals we run. we also support per-route variant mapping.
[00:05:37] Evan (Atlas CTO): in a production posture, do you recommend dedicated or hosted for us? given our compliance needs and expected steady throughput (~150 req/s)
[00:05:46] Maya (Redwood AE): short answer — Dedicated if data isolation and network egress controls are required and you need predictable CPUs/GPU; hosted is faster to market. Dedicated gives you the ability to use aggressive quantization profiles on fixed hardware and more predictable unit economics at scale. For 150 req/s with high p95 requirements, Dedicated plus persistent KV looks sensible.
[00:06:05] Priya (Atlas): cost-wise, does dedicated improve tokens/$ compared to hosted at our scale?
[00:06:10] Carlos (Redwood SE): at committed capacity yes — we modeled committed monthly pool and saw 10–18% lower unit cost for steady state workloads versus hosted list rates, plus you get reserved latency headroom. however there are commit and admin overheads to consider.
[00:06:24] Ben (SRE): anything around observability? we need token-level tracing and audit logs for compliance.
[00:06:29] Maya (Redwood AE): Redwood Console gives per-token cost breakdowns, trace ids, and full audit logs for deployments. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your SIEM — we'll include a doc link after the call.
[00:06:40] Priya (Atlas): perfect. quick question — what's the impact of caching TTL on freshness? some of our intents are time-sensitive.
[00:06:47] Carlos (Redwood SE): TTL is configurable per-intent. for time-sensitive intents you can set TTL to 30s or disable caching. we also support conditional cache invalidation hooks from your app, so you can evict on content change.
[00:06:58] Marta (Atlas): good. a couple of nitty-gritty things — what's the recommended batching config for dev vs prod?
[00:07:04] Carlos (Redwood SE): dev: small fixed window (10ms) with low max batch size to keep iteration latency low. prod: three-tier with small lane maxBatch 8/timeout 10ms, medium lane maxBatch 32/timeout 20ms, large lane maxBatch 128/timeout 40ms. you'll tune based on real concurrency.
[00:07:21] Noah (Atlas): can you quantify the CPU/GPU utilization difference between continuous and three-tier? we're hitting GPU saturation in bursts.
[00:07:28] Carlos (Redwood SE): continuous tends to smooth GPU utilization but with higher average queue length; three-tier gives more headroom for small requests so GPU can process medium+large batches more efficiently — net effect is often similar GPU cycles but lower tail queuing delays. we'll share utilization graphs.
[00:07:43] Priya (Atlas): great. now about the 72h steady-state run — we want to validate unit economics across typical weekly cyclic load. what's the experiment plan?
[00:07:51] Maya (Redwood AE): plan: run 72h with traffic replay, 1) continuous baseline, 2) three-tier baseline, 3) three-tier + persistent KV cache, 4) three-tier + quant int4 canary (small %) to check quality. We'll collect token counts, generated+input tokens, p50/p95/p99, GPU util, and cost per hour. Carlos will script it.
[00:08:11] Carlos (Redwood SE): yes we'll instrument logs and give raw CSVs. expecting about 24 hours to run the three-tier+cache and another 24 for the int4 canary.
[00:08:19] Evan (Atlas CTO): timeline for results?
[00:08:21] Maya (Redwood AE): aim to have initial results by Monday 2/9.
[00:08:25] Priya (Atlas): ok good. couple more questions — on security docs, we need SOC2 and KMS integration examples.
[00:08:32] Maya (Redwood AE): we'll send the SOC2 summary and a KMS integration guide after the call. also we'll include an example of HSM-backed key rotation we did for another customer.
[00:08:42] Marta (Atlas): thanks. any blockers from Redwood on running persistent KV?
[00:08:46] Carlos (Redwood SE): no blockers; we need an S3-compatible endpoint and small IAM role for the pilot. we can provide a temporary bucket if needed.
[00:08:55] Priya (Atlas): ok we'll decide and share details.
[00:08:59] Maya (Redwood AE): quick note on economics — if the int4 canary passes quality, the blended tokens/$ moves to ~70k tokens/$ for your mix because int4 further reduces per-token cost. that's a big delta but we need to validate sample completions thoroughly to protect quality.
[00:09:17] Noah (Atlas): how many eval prompt sets do you recommend to detect the 1% hallucination threshold?
[00:09:22] Carlos (Redwood SE): we recommend ~2k prompts covering edge cases plus a stratified sample from production. we'll run automatic scoring and flag categories where quality drifts.
[00:09:33] Evan (Atlas CTO): ok. anything else from finance or procurement side?
[00:09:36] Priya (Atlas): finance asked for a per-route cost projection for Q2 if we go dedicated. would that be possible?
[00:09:43] Maya (Redwood AE): yes we can generate a per-route cost projection after the 72h run — will include committed pool pricing scenarios and a small sensitivity analysis.
[00:09:53] Ben (SRE): on the integration side — will Redwood handle rolling updates without cache stomping, or do we need to coordinate?
[00:10:01] Carlos (Redwood SE): we can coordinate zero-downtime rollouts. persistent KV helps avoid stomping; otherwise we have warmup hooks and sequential rollout options.
[00:10:09] Priya (Atlas): great. last part — next steps recap?
[00:10:13] Maya (Redwood AE): recap: Redwood runs 72h experiments (Carlos + team), send updated cost sheet (Maya), share security docs (Maya), Atlas provides traces and SSO test accounts (Marta & Priya). schedule deep dive on Thu 2/5 for tail latency.
[00:10:29] Evan (Atlas CTO): sounds good. thanks everyone.
[00:10:33] Maya (Redwood AE): thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts. bye.

[End of call]
